title: Matsyapurana

reply:
Only 47.114 and 47.116 state kinship, and both are in Indra's speech to Jayantī.

- In 47.114 Indra calls Jayantī "svāṃ kanyām" (his own daughter), so Jayantī is the daughter of Indra. The verse calls Indra "pākaśāsana", so I use Indra as the stem.
- In 47.116, "tasya dattā'si" says she is given to Kāvya. That is a gift, not a statement of wifehood, so I do not record it as wife_of.
- In 47.113, "patnī" refers to Bhṛgu's wife, who is not named. Kāvya is not named as her husband here, and no named person is a party to the relation, so I omit it.
